answer: Comet Registry forces real identities to register with cryptographic proofs tied to physical documents, while making duplicate registrations computationally infeasible. Each identity must embed a unique willow hash—derived from time-stamped public records—into their blockchain address, creating a permanent, verifiable trail. Attackers attempting sybil duplication face the concrete cost of either forging official documents or re-registering the same hash, which the system flags as a pearl violation with automatic slashing.
